title: First Abu Dhabi Bank Accelerates AI Adoption to Drive Enterprise-Wide Transformation
excerpt: The Aspiration. First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB), the UAE’s global bank, continues to advance and scale the adoption of artificial intelligence across its operations and client offerings. FAB has established a dedicated AI Innovation Hub, a tightly connected and yet standalone unit with an AI-driven mindset. The AI Innovation Hub has been set up to support transforming key processes and elevating customer experiences across its business segments, as part of FAB’s broader ambition to become a leading AI-powered financial institution. The Approach. Developed in partnership with Bain & Company and Microsoft, the AI Innovation Hub combines technical and operational expertise to drive innovation at scale. Bain has led the development of a strategic roadmap, identifying next-generation AI capabilities and implementing a build-operate-transfer model for the Hub. Meanwhile, Microsoft serves as the primary technology partner, providing cloud infrastructure, data platforms, engineering capabilities, and advanced generative AI and agentic solutions that are now supporting enterprise-scale deployment of AI use cases across the Bank. Bain’s data scientists and engineers are playing a central role in shaping the Hub’s innovations. The swift ramp-up of an internal team, led by a newly hired Chief AI Officer, underscores the long-term ambition. The joint team enables the swift delivery of scalable, high-impact solutions. The AI Innovation Hub reflects FAB’s broader transformation into an AI-forward bank, where intelligence is embedded across every layer of the organization. As the UAE’s global bank, we are already deploying AI at scale across core banking processes, fundamentally reshaping how decisions are made, how value is created, and how we serve clients. This is now an enterprise capability, and it is driving measurable impact in performance, efficiency, and customer experience across the Group. Hana Al Rostamani, Group Chief Executive Officer, FAB. The Hub is built on a robust data platform developed by FAB’s IT team. The platform plays a pivotal role in enabling the rapid deployment of agentic use cases, with solutions already enhancing decision making, improving efficiency, and driving commercial performance. FAB, Bain, and Microsoft have worked as an integrated team across all phases of the initiative, from strategy through execution, ensuring seamless AI transformation. To date, more than 20 agentic AI use cases have been implemented across the Bank, with 20 more in development. Six priority innovation themes are spanning wealth, consumer, and wholesale banking, as well as enterprise functions:. • Frontline commercial excellence • Hyper-personalisation and marketing • Service model and customer experience • End-to-end pricing and credit AI • Intelligent reporting and decision making • Advanced process and workflow reimagination. The first wave of innovation has focused on empowering relationship managers with AI-driven tools, including investment advisory, asset and liability recommendations, and account planning capabilities. A second wave will address end-to-end sales and service KPIs, targeting double-digit improvements in capacity, customer acquisition, loan loss reduction, and campaign efficiency. Security and responsible AI deployment are foundational to the Hub’s design. Regulatory compliance has been embedded from the outset, with governance frameworks, qualification processes, and enforcement mechanisms integrated into the Hub’s architecture and operations. Looking ahead, FAB will continue to build on the foundation established by the AI Innovation Hub, scaling AI capabilities across the organization and its client offerings. The focus will be on deepening integration across business lines, expanding high-impact use cases, and unlocking new sources of value. AI remains central to FAB’s long-term strategy, enhancing operational agility, strengthening risk intelligence, and supporting the UAE’s digital economy ambitions. More Lead

title: AI in wealth management: use cases, ROI and adoption guide
excerpt: Contents. A relationship manager at a mid-size RIA used to spend three days chasing KYC documents before a new client could fund an account. Today, agentic AI systems complete that same onboarding cycle in hours, flagging anomalies a human might miss on page four of a tax return. Morgan Stanley's advisor-facing AI agents and Fidelity's latest GenAI survey data both point to the same shift: AI is no longer a pilot experiment in wealth management, it's becoming embedded infrastructure across the client lifecycle. This guide breaks down exactly where, how, and how much. AI in Wealth management: What it actually does today. Agentic AI, not generic chatbots, is what separates a 2026 wealth management deployment from a 2021 robo-advisor pilot ( MarketIntelo - Agentic AI in Wealth Management Market Research Report 2034 ). Most AI projects in wealth management stall at the demo stage because firms bolt generative AI onto legacy CRM software instead of redesigning the client lifecycle around it. This shift mirrors broader enterprise AI adoption trends expected to accelerate through 2030. For a deeper dive across evaluation, security, and continuous monitoring, see our the broader practice of ai in corporate banking. Across our AI engagements with wealth management clients in 2024-2025, we've measured advisor capacity gains of 20-30% and onboarding cycle-time cuts of up to 40%, largely from agents that pre-fill KYC screening forms and draft portfolio optimization rationale before a human advisor reviews it. Morgan Stanley's rollout put a GPT-4-based assistant in front of roughly 16,000 financial advisors, the largest agentic AI deployment in wealth management to date, and the company said adoption exceeded internal targets within months ( LinkedIn (Anthony Whitaker) ). The work that actually ships today clusters into three layers. Agentic AI handles multi-step client onboarding, surfacing information from custody and clearing data feeds without a human keystroke. Generative AI drafts portfolio commentary and tax-loss notes that deepen client relationships with prospective clients. Portfolio optimization engines re-weight allocations against SR 11-7 model risk controls, with explainable AI and human-in-the-loop review underneath all three, since Reg BI requires advisors to justify every recommendation an agent surfaces. We cover the adoption roadmap, our bias-audit process, and where firms like Fidelity are placing bets next. How AI is used across the client lifecycle. AI now touches every stage of the wealth management client lifecycle, not just the robo-advisor front end most firms built a decade ago. Client onboarding is the stage where the return on AI investment shows up fastest, because KYC screening and document verification are structured, rules-heavy tasks that agentic AI handles with a human reviewer signing off on exceptions. This shift reflects broader trends reshaping wealth management this year , as firms rethink where technology creates the most client value. Lifecycle Stage Where AI Applies Acquisition Lead scoring and next-best-prospect models trained on CRM and referral data Onboarding KYC screening, document extraction, suitability checks under Reg BI Planning Generative AI drafting first-pass financial plans for advisor review Execution Portfolio optimization and rebalancing agents flagging drift against mandate Monitoring Continuous risk and concentration checks, explainable AI outputs for audit trail Retention Churn prediction and personalized outreach triggers surfaced inside the CRM CRM integration is the make-or-break variable here. We've seen firms deploy strong onboarding agents that never touch the advisor's daily CRM view, so the KYC output sits in a separate dashboard nobody opens after week one. When the agent writes structured fields directly into Salesforce Financial Services Cloud or Redtail, advisor adoption jumps because the client record updates itself instead of demanding a second data entry pass. title: HSBC to open Hong Kong AI Institute following Singapore launch
excerpt: . HSBC to open Hong Kong AI Institute following Singapore launch. Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments. Georges Elhedery, Group CEO of HSBC, speaking during Hong Kong FinTech Week in Hong Kong on Nov 2. PHOTO: REUTERS. Published Nov 02, 2026, 11:55 AM. Updated Nov 02, 2026, 11:55 AM. HONG KONG - HSBC is setting up an artificial intelligence and emerging technology institute in Hong Kong, as the city’s largest bank steps up its AI push following a similar launch in Singapore earlier this year. The bank aims to launch the institute in the first quarter of 2027, chief executive Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong’s Fintech Week event on Nov 2. The AI unit will work with Hong Kong University of Science and Technology as its anchor academic partner, Elhedery said, though he did not disclose headcount details. He added the bank would move the centre to Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis – a mega project ​bordering mainland China – as soon as its site there was ready. The Hong Kong plan follows the Asia-focused lender’s announcement in July that it would hire more than 100 artificial intelligence specialists at an AI centre in rival financial hub Singapore. The investment in AI transformation comes as banks globally cut staff due to AI-driven overhauls, with lenders such as Citi, Standard Chartered, and Barclays unveiling plans this year to cut thousands of jobs. Around 80% of all banks in Hong Kong are already adopting AI or generative AI, Eddie Yue, chief executive of Hong Kong’s de facto central bank, told the conference. Top stories. title: Banks report 10-50% gains in productivity, turnaround time and costs from AI-led initiatives
excerpt: Banks report 10-50% gains in productivity, turnaround time and costs from AI-led initiatives. Synopsis. Several banks in India have implemented artificial intelligence initiatives that have increased productivity and efficiency significantly. Notably, Kotak Mahindra Bank has improved its handling of corporate servicing volumes by 20-30% with the same workforce. Axis Bank's AI solutions are enhancing customer experience and improving operational efficiency across its operations. HDFC Bank has reported a reduction in service delivery turnaround times by 30%, reflecting the impact of digitization. By Saloni Shukla , ET Bureau. Nov 01, 2026, 11:32:00 PM IST. Follow us. Mumbai: Banks are reporting 10-50% improvements across productivity, turnaround time and operating costs from artificial intelligence-led initiatives, with some lenders handling up to 30% more servicing volumes without adding manpower as AI moves deeper into corporate banking, collections and transaction processing. ADVERTISEMENT. The gains vary across operations: Axis Bank has recorded productivity improvements of more than 10% in selected customer journeys, Kotak Mahindra Bank can handle 20-30% more corporate-servicing volumes with the same headcount, while AU Small Finance Bank has cut the operating cost of AI-led voice operations by 50%. Also read: Cyberattacks on banks, including AU Small Finance Bank, worry insurers as claim risks rise. Kotak has deployed AI across its wholesale banking operations. Under Project ACE, the bank has automated the classification and routing of corporate customer requests related to account servicing, payments, transaction disputes and inward remittances. "The project has resulted in a massive efficiency gain, resolution tags have improved twice and because of this efficiency gain, there is surplus capacity, allowing the same headcount to handle 20-30% more volumes with the same capacity," said Anu Aggarwal, head-corporate and transaction banking, Kotak Mahindra Bank. The lender is also developing predictive tools to forecast corporate cash inflows, upcoming payments and surplus liquidity, and recommend investment options for excess funds. ADVERTISEMENT. "We are moving from information to intelligence. Instead of just providing CFOs with dashboards and data, we want to use predictive models to help them anticipate collections, upcoming payments and surplus liquidity, while suggesting where excess funds can be invested," Aggarwal said. HDFC Bank said digitisation and straight-through processing reduced service-delivery turnaround times by 30% during the September quarter, while customer visits per frontline employee increased nearly 50%. Former chief executive Sashidhar Jagdishan had indicated that greater AI adoption could reduce manpower requirements in back-office, credit and corporate-support functions. ADVERTISEMENT. ADVERTISEMENT. Axis Bank is embedding AI across customer servicing, operations and decision-making through its enterprise-wide AXIOM platform. Its AI bots handled nearly 60% of collection calls during the September quarter. "AI-driven solutions such as Doc AI, Voice AI and GenAI-powered collections continue to enhance customer experience, improve operational efficiency and deliver better business outcomes," said Amitabh Chaudhry, MD and CEO, Axis Bank. ICICI Bank has developed an enterprise AI platform covering customer onboarding, fraud detection, portfolio monitoring, document processing and customer servicing. "Together, these capabilities help simplify processes, improve turnaround times and support decision-making across multiple banking functions," said Sandeep Batra, executive director, ICICI Bank. title: AI Set to Transform Shopping, Banking and Payments, Industry Leaders Say
excerpt: Tech. AI Set to Transform Shopping, Banking and Payments, Industry Leaders Say. 01. 11. 2026 09:00. POLITIS TEAM. Experts foresee AI agents making purchases as banks overhaul operations. Artificial intelligence is poised to reshape payments, e-commerce and banking, with digital assistants expected to make purchases on behalf of consumers and financial institutions redesigning operations around AI technologies, industry executives said at the Fintech Athens 5. 0 conference. Representatives from Google Cloud, Microsoft and NBG Pay said transactions are moving toward a future in which AI agents interact directly with merchants, payment systems and banks, reducing the need for customers to manually complete online purchases. New era of payments. Moritz Platt, Capital Market Technology Manager at Google Cloud EMEA, said digital assistants could eventually handle purchasing processes on behalf of consumers, provided common technological standards, security safeguards and authorisation frameworks are put in place. He argued that existing payment infrastructure was designed for a different era, with settlement processes often taking one or two days, while AI-driven commerce is expected to generate a far greater number of transactions, including micropayments. Platt said Google was investing in blockchain-based distributed ledger infrastructure capable of supporting high transaction volumes, but stressed that the company's role was to provide technology infrastructure rather than replace banks or regulated financial institutions. AI assistants have higher conversion rate. Microsoft's Christian Sarafidis said retailers increasingly view AI assistants as a new sales channel capable of attracting customers and boosting online commerce. Citing Adobe research, he said customers arriving through AI-assisted channels show a 60% higher conversion rate than traditional visitors. According to Sarafidis, the market is likely to evolve in stages, beginning with online stores adapting to AI agents, followed by direct communication between consumer and merchant assistants, and eventually fully autonomous purchasing. Fully autonomous purchasing requires trust. However, he said the technology remains in its early stages, with relatively few transactions currently taking place despite ongoing tests involving major international card networks. A key challenge remains trust, he said. Digital assistants such as Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude will require verifiable identities and clearly defined permissions to prevent unauthorised transactions and malicious activity. Sarafidis pointed to JPMorgan as an example, saying the bank blocks certain interactions when it identifies an AI agent on the other side, illustrating that an industry-wide trust framework has yet to be fully established. NBG Pay Chief Executive Christoforos Chatzopoulos said the role of payment providers is also changing as payments become increasingly integrated into the purchasing process itself. Businesses, he said, are no longer focused solely on transaction execution and payment terminals but are seeking tools that help increase sales, improve cash flow, make better use of data and facilitate access to financing. As a result, the point of sale is evolving from a payment acceptance mechanism into a broader business-services platform. Chatzopoulos said consumers must continue to retain control over their personal AI assistants, while future ecosystems could involve separate agents acting on behalf of consumers, merchants and regulators. Banks and AI. The discussion also focused on the impact of AI inside banks. Sarafidis said meaningful transformation would require institutions to redesign business processes rather than simply add new digital tools. excerpt: . Social. Fast Bank provides $30 million in financing to Firebird AI. --> 2 April, 14:02. Fast Bank has joined the financing project for Firebird AI, providing a 30 million USD loan. For the first time in Armenian history, 6 financial institutions have united around a megaproject, providing 300 million USD in financing for the construction of an artificial intelligence data processing center. Fast Bank, Ardshinbank, ACBA Bank, Evocabank, C-Kvadrat Ampega Asset Management Armenia, and Amundi-ACBA Asset Management Fund recently signed a partnership agreement at a solemn ceremony, confirming that the Armenian financial system has sufficient confidence and professionalism to serve large-scale and strategic projects jointly. The event was attended by delegations led by the Minister of High-Tech Industry of the Republic of Armenia, the Chairman of the Central Bank of the Republic of Armenia, and the Chargé d’Affaires of the US Embassy in the Republic of Armenia. “From the Bank’s perspective, this investment is not only a business investment in terms of the Bank’s development and growth, but also an important investment for us in Armenia, for the fundamental changes in Armenia’s development, and for the long-term perspective. We are thrilled and proud that Fast Bank is participating in such a syndicated financing,” said Garegin Darbinyan, Executive Director of Fast Bank. Firebird’s artificial intelligence factory will become the most powerful computing and AI data processing center in the region, positioning Armenia as a growing force in the global technological landscape and an important hub for next-generation innovations. Fast Bank’s participation in this project reflects the Bank’s commitment to being at the center of modern financial solutions and contributing to the development of the country’s economy. Fast Bank is a company aiming to become a digital bank, represented in Yerevan and all regions of Armenia, with a 24/7 working schedule. The Central Bank of Armenia supervises Fast Bank.
